title: 730. The Salting-out of Non-electrolytes. Part II. The Effect of Variation in Non-electrolyte (T. J. Morrison and F. Billett)
experimental_method: Flow-film gas-solubility apparatus (Part I) with separate gas burette and absorption spiral; solvents degassed by a vapour-pump principle; gas volume against solvent volume slope.
uncertainties_stated: not stated for gas solubilities (liquid solubilities of aromatics: ~0.5 % benzene/toluene, 1-2 % ethylbenzene).
quality_remarks: Water solubilities (Table 2) are measured; the salt solutions were only reported through derived Setschenow-type salting-out constants (Table 3), not as individual solubilities. Concentrations of salt solutions were 'about 1 g.-equiv. per 1000 g of water' with small corrections via the Setschenow equation. Gas preparations from several sources gave identical results within error (N2, O2, H2).
not_extracted_tables: Table 1 (intercepts I and hydration numbers, derived)

Table 3 (salting-out constants k = (log s0/s)/c for salts NaCl, LiCl, KI, KCl, HCl, BaCl2, LaCl3 at four values of 1/T, derived by the authors; the underlying solubilities in salt solutions are not tabulated)
Table 3 lower block (benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene at 25 C in NaCl solution: liquid hydrocarbons, out of scope, and k derived)
